title: Subprograms: procedures and functions
sub: Worksheet for the 360° experience: Assembly line
objectives: know how to define a subprogram with def and how to call it
understand how a parameter passes a value into a subprogram and how return passes one back out
know the difference between a local variable and a global one
starter: A program defines a subprogram called banner with one print line inside it, and then stops. Nothing is printed when it runs. Explain why, and write down the line that has been left out.

stations.name: Writing a procedure
stations.fact: Writing a job once and calling it many times has a name of its own: code reuse.
stations.challenge: What is the difference between defining a procedure and calling it?

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: Ask the user for a word. Write a procedure called finish that prints done, then display [word] and call finish, so the word comes first.
Ask the user for two words, one on each line. Write a procedure called rule that prints =====, then display the rule, the first word, the rule, the second word and the rule, one on each line.

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Parameters
stations.fact: The names in the definition are the parameters; the values handed over when it is called are the arguments.
stations.challenge: Why is a procedure with a parameter more useful than one without?

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: Ask the user for two words, one on each line. Write a procedure called show that takes one word and prints value [that word]. Call it once for each word, in the order they were typed.
Ask the user for two whole numbers, one on each line. Write a procedure called product that takes both and prints total [the first times the second]. Call it, and print nothing else.

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Returning a value
stations.fact: return ends the subprogram there and then, so any line written after it never runs.
stations.challenge: Why would a task insist a subprogram returns a value rather than prints it?

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: Ask the user for a whole number. Write a function called double that returns twice its parameter and prints nothing at all, then display [what double hands back] and nothing else.

Ask the user for a whole number. Write a function called sign that returns the word up for a number above 0, down for a number below 0 and flat for 0, and display [what sign hands back] and nothing else.

Ask the user for two whole numbers, one on each line. Write a function called area that returns the first times the second and holds no print at all. Store what it returns and display one line, area [that value].

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Functions and procedures
stations.fact: The exam marks this difference, so say 'function' only when a value actually comes back.
stations.challenge: Decide whether each subprogram in your program is a function or a procedure.

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: Ask the user for a word and then a whole number. Write a function called tag that returns high for a number of 40 or more and low below 40, and a procedure called show that displays [word]: [that returned word]. Use both, and print one line only.

Ask the user for two whole numbers, one on each line. Write a function called larger that returns the bigger of its two parameters and a procedure called announce that displays largest [that value]. Use both, and print one line only.

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Local and global
stations.fact: Keeping variables local is good practice: it stops one part of a program quietly breaking another.
stations.challenge: Why can two subprograms both use a variable called total without clashing?

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: Ask the user for a whole number and keep it in a variable called total. Write a procedure called boost with a local total of its own, set to 99, that prints it. Call boost, then display [the main total] on the next line.

Ask the user for a whole number and keep it in a variable called count. Write a procedure called bump that takes one whole number, adds 1 to its parameter and prints the result. Call bump with count, then display [count] on the next line.

Write a procedure called up that adds 3 to a shared total and a procedure called down that adds 1 to the same total. Ask the user for a whole number of turns, call up and then down once per turn, and display [the final total] and nothing else.

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Putting it together
stations.fact: Breaking a problem into named parts is decomposition, which you met in topic 2.1.
stations.challenge: Plan which parts of a booking receipt program should become subprograms.

rows: Write a function called score that returns 3 for a number of 2 or more, 1 for a number of 1 and 0 for 0. Ask the user for how many numbers there are, then for that many whole numbers, one on each line. Display [everything score hands back, added up] and nothing else.

Ask the user for two whole numbers, one on each line. Write a function called base that returns the first number times 25, a function called whole that calls base and returns what base gave times the second number, plus 10, and a procedure called report that calls whole and displays first [the first number], then whole [that value] on the next line.

keyq: When should a subprogram return a value rather than print one?
exam: A subprogram called vat takes an amount and its last line is print(amount * 0.2). The main program writes tax = vat(50) and then prints tax, which shows None. Explain why, and write the change needed inside the subprogram.
Write a function that takes a length and a width in metres and returns the area, and a main program that uses it to print the area of two different rooms.
Write a procedure that takes a pupil's name and a score and prints one tidy line of a results table, then call it for three different pupils.
